transcript:
Date/Time: 2027-09-07T15:00:00Z
Duration: 00:42:00
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Arjun Patel (Redwood SE), Lena Ortiz (Echelon Head of ML), David Kim (Echelon Infra), Priya Singh (Echelon Security)

Summary: quick integration discovery to understand Echelon's stack (LangChain/LlamaIndex usage), requirements for hosted vs dedicated vs private, gateway/proxy and rate limit patterns, and observability hooks for production monitoring. Agreed to run a POC with benchmark scripts and share pricing + security docs.

Topics: SDKs and client libs; LangChain/LlamaIndex integration; gateway/proxy placement; rate limits & quotas; observability and tracing hooks; data residency and KMS; pilot scope and success criteria.

Transcript:
[00:00] Maya Chen: hey everyone, thanks for joining, i'll hand off to arjun to do a quick technical check then we'll go through questions, sound good?
[00:05] Arjun Patel: yeah thanks maya. hi lena, david, priya. quick context - redwood supports hosted api, dedicated reserved pools and private vpc/on-prem installs. today we want to understand how you integrate - SDKs, langchain, where you want to put gateway or proxy, and your observability needs.
[00:18] Lena Ortiz: cool thanks. high level we run an nlp platform that uses langchain + llmaindex, mostly retrieval augmented generation for clinical summarization. currently prototypes use hosted openai but we're hitting rate limits and cost spikes. main asks: latency under 150ms p95 for short responses, per-customer data isolation, and SOC2/compliance.
[00:34] David Kim: infra note - we route all external models through an internal gateway/proxy so we can enforce auth, per-tenant quotas and audit logging. we'll need either a supported proxy config or a private endpoint in our vpc.
[00:45] Priya Singh: from security, key points: audit logs, KMS integration (customer-managed keys ideal), SSO (SAML), and clear data residency controls. also need encryption in transit + at rest and a SOC2 attestation.
[01:02] Arjun Patel: got it. for the langchain/llamaindex side we have first-class SDKs and examples. we ship python and js clients and a set of connectors - there are example chains for langchain and routines for llamaindex. we can share a sample repo that shows streaming, function-calls, and structured outputs.
[01:20] Lena Ortiz: can those SDKs plug into our existing chaining? we heavily use langchain agents and LlamaIndex document stores.
[01:25] Arjun Patel: yes - we have connectors that subclass the LLM interface. some customers use the redwood python client directly with LangChain's OpenAI wrapper by providing the redwood model endpoint; others wrap it in a local proxy to enforce tenant routing. small caveat: sometimes the model name mapping is slightly different so you'll see model aliases, e.g., redwood-4x vs rwd-4x in examples - transcription errors sometimes.
[01:42] David Kim: about placing the gateway - we want control plane calls to be out-of-band. can we deploy a sidecar/proxy, or do you provide a managed gateway?
[01:49] Maya Chen: two options. Hosted customers call redwood's public api; you can put your internal gateway in front of it. For Dedicated we can place a customer-dedicated endpoint in your vpc that your gateway talks to directly. For Private on-prem we ship a package you run behind your firewall with a control plane that talks to redwood for metadata (optional).
[02:05] David Kim: what about rate limits and quotas? we need per-tenant quotas and burst control; also need predictable throttling behavior.
[02:12] Arjun Patel: we support token and request-based quotas. For hosted you can configure per-api-key quotas and rate-limit policies; for Dedicated we mirror via our control plane and you can enforce quotas at your infra layer too. Docs include examples for leaky-bucket style throttling and how to expose 429 responses for graceful backoff. we'll share the rate-limit policy doc.
[02:30] Priya Singh: observability - we need traces, per-call latency, token counts, and cost metadata. how mature are your hooks?
[02:37] Arjun Patel: Redwood Console exposes per-route token breakdowns, p95 latency, and per-key cost. We provide tracing integrations (OpenTelemetry) and can emit spans with request_id and model variant info. You can ingest logs into your splunk/datadog via webhook or export. For PII-sensitive workloads we can redact payloads and still emit token-level metrics.
[02:56] Lena Ortiz: curious about memory/KV cache behavior - RAG performance depends a lot on fast KV cache retrieval and prefix caching. how does dedicated vs hosted affect latency here?
[03:05] Arjun Patel: good question. Hosted has distributed cache across our infra; p95 is usually higher than a colocated dedicated pool. Dedicated capacity gives you local KV cache and better cold-start behavior. Private on-prem obviously gives you the lowest network latency but requires you to manage nodes and occasionally kernel/patch updates. we'll put some numbers in the TCO slide.
[03:26] Lena Ortiz: and quantization? some of our team runs 4-bit quant models to save cost. do you support quantized model variants?
[03:32] Arjun Patel: yes - runtime supports int8/4 quantized variants; we recommend testing quality vs perf. Redwood Optimize can recommend quantization profiles based on your workload and expected quality thresholds.
[03:42] David Kim: about integration - we'll likely want a proxy that enforces per-customer routing and records detailed audit logs. Do you support per-tenant keys or per-tenant endpoints?
[03:52] Maya Chen: For Dedicated we can provision separate endpoints per team or namespace; for Hosted you can get per-api-key separation and tags for billing/observability. Private gives full isolation with customer-managed networking.
[04:03] Priya Singh: KMS - can we bring our own key (BYOK)?
[04:06] Arjun Patel: yes, we support customer-managed keys via KMS/HSM integrations for Dedicated and Private. Hosted supports managed keys with the option to integrate with customer KMS for some enterprise contracts.
[04:18] Lena Ortiz: success criteria for a pilot: validate latency at 95th under 150ms for a 300 token response, observe token-level cost within budget, and confirm integration with LangChain flows and our proxy.
[04:29] Maya Chen: sounds straightforward. Our recommended pilot: 2-week POC using a dedicated small pool or hosted reserved burst capacity, run benchmark scripts (we'll provide) against your actual requests, and a joint evaluation on quality/latency/cost.
[04:40] David Kim: what's your suggested throughput for the pilot? we expect bursts up to 50 RPS across tenants, steady state maybe 8-10 RPS.
[04:47] Arjun Patel: for those numbers we'd recommend a small dedicated pod (N GPUs) - i'll size and send a suggested config. We'll also include a hosted baseline for comparison.
[04:57] Priya Singh: compliance docs - can you share SOC2 report and your data retention policy?
[05:02] Maya Chen: yes we'll share SOC2 audit report summary and the security whitepaper. We'll flag areas around data residency and retention and show how redwood's retention defaults can be adjusted for enterprise customers.
[05:15] Lena Ortiz: quick question on SDKs - do you support streaming token-by-token in python? Our UI shows progressive typing so streaming is important.
[05:21] Arjun Patel: yes we support streaming responses in python and js SDKs; examples include handling partial deltas and reconnect logic. We also have function-calling style structured outputs for downstream parsing.
[05:34] Maya Chen: any other blockers from your side?
[05:37] David Kim: licensing and procurement will need pricing of Dedicated monthly commit vs hosted per-token and an estimate of overage costs.
[05:44] Priya Singh: plus a list of sub processors and our legal team will want a DPA and data processing details.
[05:50] Maya Chen: we'll include those in the packet.
[05:53] Lena Ortiz: one more - open source model support: we use some community models, will you support bringing my own model artifact if we go private?
[05:59] Arjun Patel: for Private on-prem yes you can bring and run your own model artifacts; for Dedicated we can onboard vetted open models into your pool, and for Hosted we have a curated catalog but can discuss custom model onboarding for enterprise accounts.
[06:12] Maya Chen: recap - redwood to send pricing + dedicated sizing, SE to send POC scripts and langchain/llamaindex examples, security to send SOC2 and KMS docs, and customer to share sample workload and confirm internal recipients for compliance questionnaire. next meeting we'll review the POC runbook.
[06:28] Lena Ortiz: perfect, thanks everyone.
[06:31] Maya Chen: thank you, we'll follow up with all materials by next week.

Notes on audio/transcription quality: occasional name mis-attributions, some product names garbled (e.g., rwd-4x vs redwood-4x), filler words and crosstalk.
